clusters.name: Strain / solid‑state deformation transducers
clusters.description: Converts localized bending, compression or bulk deformation directly into electrical energy via solid‑state material effects (piezoelectric, flexoelectric). Suited for small high‑strain spots producing charge/voltage from material deformation.

clusters.name: Triboelectric / contact‑friction transducers
clusters.description: Harvests charge through repeated contact, separation, or sliding of dissimilar surfaces (triboelectric effect). Core active ingredient is surface charge transfer rather than bulk material strain.

clusters.name: Electromagnetic induction transducers
clusters.description: Converts relative motion between magnets and coils into AC electrical power via changing magnetic flux; used standalone or driven by moving masses, cranks or limb linkages.

clusters.name: Electrostatic / variable‑capacitance transducers
clusters.description: Converts mechanical deformation into electrical energy by changing capacitor geometry or electrode separation, often requiring charge prebiasing or charge transfer circuits.

clusters.name: Inertial / oscillatory harvesters (moving mass)
clusters.description: Uses proof masses, pendulums, impacts or oscillatory masses to convert translational or vibrational body motion into relative motion that drives a transducer. Focuses on inertial motion as the core energy source.

clusters.name: Mechanical motion conversion & accumulation
clusters.description: Linkages, gearboxes, ratchets, cams, belts and compliant elements that convert, scale, accumulate or smooth intermittent human motion into generator‑friendly torque/speed or continuous rotation.

clusters.name: Motion‑phase gating & one‑way engagement
clusters.description: Clutches, one‑way couplings, pawls and phase‑gating mechanisms that selectively engage harvesting during beneficial motion phases to reduce parasitic loss and maximize net energy.

clusters.name: Elastic energy storage and timing elements
clusters.description: Springs, elastic elements, compliant pads and mechanisms that store, smooth, time‑shift or release mechanical energy to match harvester timing or buffer intermittent inputs.

clusters.name: Hydraulic / pneumatic pressure capture & reservoir
clusters.description: Converts deformation into pressurized fluid (air or liquid) stored in a reservoir and released to drive turbines, pistons or generators; includes wearable pump concepts.

clusters.name: Body‑mounted interfaces and distributed harvesters
clusters.description: Localized mounts, compression pads, cranks or multiple small limb units that couple joint or limb displacement to harvesting hardware; emphasizes placement, comfort and mechanical coupling.

clusters.name: Flexible substrate & integration for wearables
clusters.description: Embedding harvesters, conductors and interconnects into textiles, elastomers or flexible substrates for conformal, low‑profile wearable energy capture and user comfort.

clusters.name: Thermal and bioelectric harvesters
clusters.description: Continuous, low‑power sources using skin‑to‑ambient thermoelectric modules or galvanic/skin‑potential electrodes to harvest thermal gradients or biopotential differences.

clusters.name: Power electronics, buffering and energy routing
clusters.description: Rectifiers, impedance‑matching, MPPT/regulation, converters and short‑term buffers (supercapacitors, flywheels) that condition, store and deliver harvested energy to loads or batteries.

clusters.name: Sensing, control and user feedback interfaces
clusters.description: Motion sensing, algorithms, control policies, and local user feedback (LED/haptic/status) that detect motion phases, manage harvesting, and present system state to the wearer.
